question: Who is regarded as the father of local self - government in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Ripon**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord Ripon is known in India as the father of local self-government.
 
• He is known as the father of local self-government because he passed a resolution of local self-government which laid the democratic forms of municipal governance in India in 1882.
 
• The Municipal Institutions that had grown up in the country since the British Crown occupied India developed his local self-government scheme.
 
• He was the viceroy and Governor-General of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Warren Hastings (1773-1785):
 
 
• First Governor-General of Bengal, overseeing the early consolidation of British rule in India.
 
• He Reformed the judicial system by setting up civil and criminal courts (diwani and faujdari courts).
 
• Faced impeachment in Britain for alleged corruption but was acquitted after a long trial.
 
 
 
• Lord Canning (1856-1862):
 
 
• The last Governor-General and the first Viceroy of India after the Government of India Act, 1858.
 
• He Managed the aftermath of the Revolt of 1857, known for his policy of clemency toward rebels.
 
• He Introduced significant reforms, including the Indian Penal Code and the foundation of modern civil service.
 
 
 
• Lord Cornwallis (1786-1793):
 
 
• He Introduced the Permanent Settlement of Bengal in 1793, fixing land revenue and granting landlords hereditary rights.
 
• He is Reformed the administration and judiciary, introducing the Cornwallis Code, which professionalized civil services.
 
• He Played a significant role in the Third Anglo-Mysore War against Tipu Sultan, leading to British victories in southern India.
